title: Natural Q&A #4
summary: NH announces he is being forced to monetize the channel because of YouTube's new policy, then answers non-training questions: losing passion, discipline, stoicism, religion, language learning, fights, grief, straight-edge living, tattoos and why natural bodybuilding needs its own conditioning standards.
claims: YouTube's new guideline lets it run ads on unmonetized channels, so he will monetize himself to keep ads short and controlled rather than let YouTube flood his videos
He never wanted to make money from the channel; its purpose is sharing knowledge and building a community of natural lifters
He has been eligible to monetize for six months (1,000 subs and 4,000 watch hours) but chose not to
Small channels cannot grow on YouTube in 2020: the algorithm doesn't recommend them and search hides them
He listens to educational talks during warm-ups and volume work and keeps music only for hard sets, because that hypes him up more
He does about two hours of non-fitness YouTube a day and no longer watches fitness YouTube
He did judo from about age 5 to 7-8, reached orange belt, and quit after an opponent pulled his hair to avoid throws and the referee ignored it
Don't fixate on how much muscle a novice or intermediate should gain in a year; just train consistently, because by progressing you will build a good body
People who claim 15 years of training often stalled for 9 of them
As a teen he trained obsessively for football (5am sprints, two hours of dumbbells after class) and lost his love for it once matches kept being forfeited
Losing a passion is worse than never having one; his top priority is never falling out of love with bodybuilding, which he has done for 10 years and wants for 50 more
He refuses to make money from bodybuilding because turning it into a job would make it a chore and kill his love for it
When you love something, keep it the way it is; changing its nature changes your love for it
He keeps his name off the channel so he can't profit from it and wants to be a guide, not a guru
He waits a week before answering comments because many arrive late and YouTube stops notifying him
If YouTube fitness confuses or depresses you, stop watching, including his videos; your mental state matters most
If you keep progressing you are not spinning your wheels; once you know the basic programming principles you don't need more videos
Your personal experience is more valuable than his experience or all the science, because it is what works for you
He is a baptized Catholic who reads scripture his own way and does not practise in church, which he sees as an institution laid on top of the faith
He would teach if he didn't work in AI; he is still a French teacher
Discipline is not genetic; claiming it is is a cop-out used either by undisciplined people or by disciplined people flexing
Discipline is shaped by parents, peers and environment but can be learned at any age; it is the path to true happiness
He was academically disciplined thanks to his immigrant family's emphasis on school, but physically weak until he forced himself to train
Motivation is fleeting and gets you going; discipline keeps you going. Build it by imitating disciplined people
He doesn't join ideologies; he practises stoicism because it fits his introverted, controlled nature without calling himself a stoic
To learn a language: watch shows nightly with subtitles then without, practise speaking, immerse yourself, and read books while noting vocabulary
Two months speaking English in America taught him more than two years of practising alone at home
He was bullied and beaten at 12-13; once he hit back, bullies stopped because they only respect strength
Don't start with a definite physique goal; you might stop when you reach it. Just train and see
He has surpassed the anime physiques that first motivated him; his 15-year-old self would never have believed it
Skinny people can become as big as him or bigger; being told you'll be skinny forever is nonsense
Grief comes in waves that become smaller and further apart; don't use alcohol or drugs to escape it because it comes back stronger
He is straight edge: no drugs, alcohol or even painkillers (he refused them with broken ribs); his only exception is an occasional glass of red wine
He sees PEDs as hard drugs that destroy lives, which is why he is so against them
Tattoos are bad for bodybuilding: they hurt muscle definition and hide vascularity
Sobriety is just optimal health, not a personality; don't build your identity around being straight edge
Only pursue a degree or PhD with a clear idea of the jobs it leads to; academia has few jobs
Natural bodybuilders shouldn't be judged by enhanced conditioning standards; asking naturals to step on stage at 8% makes them look skeletal
Naturals should compete at around 12-15% body fat, looking big and inspiring
If pro bodybuilding had never existed, natural bodybuilding would be huge; most people find enhanced physiques disgusting
Natural shows should use the aesthetic poses of the 1950s-60s rather than mass poses naturals can't fill
